title: The Popular Get More Popular: Auditing Brand Bias in Generative Search
abstract: arXiv:2611.07614v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The shift from traditional to generative search has fundamentally transformed online product discovery. Because conversational recommendations synthesize choices into a few direct answers, subtle systemic preferences toward specific providers can exert profound commercial impacts. In this work, we audit this phenomenon through two distinct dimensions: (i) brand popularity bias, the systematic preference for market-dominant entities over long-tail alternatives, and (ii) brand familiarity bias, the ranking advantage an entity encoded in an LLM's parametric memory holds over an unfamiliar competitor. First, evaluating commercial queries across major engines, we observe persistent brand popularity bias: dominant brands in the top quintile are cited 1.4x to 2.8x more frequently than the average brand within a sample of 1,176 top market players, already present in parametric memory that external web retrieval fails to mitigate. translated_title: 强者愈强：生成式搜索中的品牌偏见审计
translated_abstract: 从传统搜索向生成式搜索的转变从根本上改变了线上产品发现的方式。由于对话式推荐将众多选择综合为少数几个直接答案，对特定提供商的微妙系统性偏好可能产生深远的商业影响。在这项工作中，我们从两个不同的维度对这一现象进行审计：(i) 品牌流行度偏见，即相对于长尾替代品牌，对市场主导品牌的系统性偏好；(ii) 品牌熟悉度偏见，即实体凭借其编码在大语言模型参数记忆中的信息相对于不为人熟知的竞争对手所拥有的排名优势。首先，通过评估各大主流引擎上的商业查询，我们观察到持续存在的品牌流行度偏见：在1,176个头部市场参与者样本中，位于最高五分位的主导品牌被引用的频率是平均品牌的1.4倍至2.8倍，这种偏见已经存在于参数记忆之中，而外部网络检索无法缓解这一问题。
tldr: 生成式搜索存在系统性品牌偏见：头部热门品牌被引用的频率是平均品牌的1.4至2.8倍，这种偏见源自模型参数记忆且无法通过外部网络检索缓解。
en_tdlr: Generative search engines exhibit persistent brand popularity bias, citing dominant brands 1.4x to 2.8x more frequently than average brands—a bias embedded in parametric memory that external web retrieval fails to mitigate.
